text:
Nora (Content): Hey team — I pushed a near-final draft of the launch blog into the doc, focused on the benchmark narrative + call-to-action for the webinar. Can folks scan for claim accuracy, legal flags, and a sharp hero?

Jamal (Growth): taking a look now. quick note: any absolute performance/cost claims need source links. if we say "40% lower per-token cost" we should link to the benchmark appendix or say "up to 40%". also prefer a short CTA for demo+webinar signup, not two CTAs. :+1:

Sam (PM): +1 on single CTA. also let's call out Dedicated briefly — customers ask about reserved capacity in the first section. maybe one sentence: "Available hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options."

Leo (Eng): saw the latency numbers in the appendix — they're from internal perf lab with batch=1, seq=512 on A100s. we should either note the test conditions or change phrasing to "internal lab results (A100, batch=1, seq=512)". avoid blanket "real-world latency" statements.

Emily (Legal): quick pass: avoid superlatives like "industry-leading" unless marketing has evidence. any customer names used in examples need signed approval. please add a citation line for the benchmarks and mark the dataset used. i'll review the final claims; ping me once the numbers are locked.

Olivia (Marketing): hero/header candidates in the doc. My preference: short + benefit-first. examples: "Predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference for production apps" or "Ship LLM features with consistent latency and lower unit costs". which resonates?

seo-bot: Suggested focus keywords: "LLM inference platform", "low-latency inference", "inference cost optimization". meta description suggestion (150 chars): "High-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and cost controls — hosted, dedicated, or private. Register for the launch webinar."

Jamal (Growth): for lead routing: let's route webinar signups to HubSpot list "launch-webinar-2026" + trigger a workflow that tags requests with "benchmark-interest" if they click the benchmark CTA. can someone confirm the form fields we need? name, company, role, region, use-case checkbox.

Nora (Content): thanks — adding an inline note about test conditions per Leo and a citation placeholder per Emily. For the CTA copy I'm leaning toward: "See the benchmarks + join our launch webinar" (single button). here's a short hero paragraph we can swap in: 

```
Redwood Inference gives engineering teams predictable LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — reducing per-token cost and keeping latency consistent at scale. Join our launch webinar to see benchmark results and a live demo.
```

Sam (PM): that hero paragraph is clear. request: can we add a 1-sentence customer outcome under the hero (no real names) e.g., "Early customers cut inference cost by up to 35% after switching to Redwood's optimized serving runtime." mark as anonymized case study.

Emily (Legal): anonymized outcome is ok as long as it's framed "early customers reported" and we keep "up to" language. add the source tag when you publish.

Leo (Eng): if we use "up to 35%" include the hardware/config note in the appendix. also suggest a tiny tech blur: "optimized kernels, KV caching, and smart routing reduce token compute waste."

Olivia (Marketing): timeline check — can we lock copy by EOD tomorrow? need final for email and landing. also want two hero variants for A/B. Jamal — can you confirm form + routing by noon?

Jamal (Growth): I can confirm routing by 12:00 PT. I also want a small benchmark explainer (one collapsible section) so readers don't get lost in numbers.

Nora (Content): plan: i'll make edits (legal citations, lab notes, single CTA, add anonymized outcome) and post an updated snippet in this thread when done. target EOD tomorrow for final review. thanks all! :rocket:
